newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsair seeks Antananarivo cargo traffic rights.
newsitem.headline: Corsair seeks Antananarivo cargo traffic rights.

text.p: Corsair said it had submitted an application to the French civil aviation authorities for air cargo traffic rights to two new destinations in the Indian Ocean.

"Since the beginning of November, our existing Boeing 747 passenger service between Paris and Reunion makes a weekly stopover at the Madagascan city of Antananarivo," a Corsair official told Reuters. Corsair is part of the Nouvelles Frontieres travel group.
Corsair also plans to launch a new, weekly 747 passenger service between Paris and Moroni, the capital of the Comoros Islands, also in the Indian Ocean, from December 17, the official said.
"We hope to receive a favourable response from the French authorities to our request for air cargo traffic rights to these two destinations by early 1997," he added.
Air France and Air Madagascar operate scheduled passenger services between Paris and Antananarivo while the French carrier also has a weekly full-freighter service to the island.
Air France is the only airline to offer a direct service from Paris to the Comoros, operating a weekly 747-200 combi on the route.
However, it plans to suspend the service from January 8 1997, an Air France official said.
Dubai government-owned airline, Emirates, carries freight from Paris and Nice to Comoros via its three-times weekly Airbus 310 passenger services to Dubai.
Corsair's cargo sales agent, Aero Cargo International, said it had made provisional plans to open a cargo office in Moroni, the capital of the Comoros Islands in the Indian Ocean, early next year.
Aero Cargo already has cargo offices on the Indian Ocean island of Reunion.

"The vast majority of freight on the Paris-Comoros route is in the form of personal effects with people moving to the islands from France and vice versa and we see scope to develop this kind of traffic," an Aero Cargo official told Reuters. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+44 171 542-5017
